events.rationale: Prompted repository/code analysis before clarification, especially tracing ordinary, sub-agent, heartbeat, cron, and background-fork permission paths instead of asking the Owner to resolve technically knowable facts.
Supported recommending and documenting a PA-only product scope, keeping Coding CLI unchanged and avoiding adjacent expansion.
Helped keep scenarios focused on operator-observable model routing, startup failure, fallback behavior, and unchanged product behavior rather than internal functions or interfaces.
This run produced a Gate 1 spec, not a design document or design-completeness review.
The change had no UI prototype or interaction-design deliverable.
A product-neutral lower-layer capability was mentioned only after the Owner explicitly requested it; the memory did not drive that decision.
The repository architecture and Owner reply directly established the PA product boundary and possibility of a product-neutral lower layer.
The change was classified as a feature, not a pure refactor or migration.
The frozen task allowed only the spec phase, so implementation workflow and engineering safeguards were out of scope.
No skill, agent instruction, runbook, or process document was authored.
No architecture review or review checklist was performed.
This was a feature request, not a regression diagnosis or bug-fix acceptance task.
Compatibility behavior was decided explicitly by the Owner: omission must preserve per-run model reuse. No migration or protocol fallback judgment was made from memory.
The task did not add discovered capabilities to an explicit saved selection or alter enable/disable sets.

It informed the initial fail-loud/no-silent-fallback framing, but the Owner supplied stronger, more specific behavior: invalid catalog entries fail startup; runtime failure retries the same model and then follows the existing permission-failure path, without a new manual-approval rule.
Failure handling was relevant, but the spec deliberately preserved the existing permission-failure semantics per Owner instruction rather than defining new feedback or recovery behavior.
The feature did not change approval cards, tool timelines, or execution-state presentation.
No subprocess, listener, worker lifecycle, or shutdown ownership behavior was in scope.
The document defined product scenarios, not an E2E test plan or critical-path catalog.
No IM message or chat UX was designed or reviewed.
Running-session steering and concurrent input behavior were unrelated to classifier-model selection.
No timestamps, provenance, routing envelopes, or model-only message metadata were introduced.
Local repository state was used as authority, but this was already mandated more strongly by the task envelope prohibiting network and outside-workspace access.
The spec required that operators can observe which model handled classification, but it did not prescribe logging fields, telemetry, or prompt-content policy.
